back: The way in which the operand of an instruction is used to find the data it works on.
The operand is the value itself, e.g. LDM #7; no memory access for the operand.
The operand is the address of the data, e.g. LDD Total.
The operand is the address of a pointer that holds the address of the data, e.g. LDI Ptr (two reads).
Effective address = operand + contents of IX, e.g. LDX Table.
Next instruction address = address of the instruction + offset.
The address actually used by an instruction after the addressing mode has been applied.
Code that works wherever it is loaded, as when relative jumps are used.
Constants: immediate. Variables: direct. Pointers: indirect. Arrays: indexed. Branches: relative.
